items.title: Coordination-Mediated Decoupling-Reconstruction Enables Semisolid Phase Regeneration of Spent Cathodes
authors: Pengrong Zhang, Yan Wang, Tingzhou Yang, Yunjie Cui, Xia Sun, Xiaoyi Zhang, Haodi Dong, Chunyong Liang, and Zhongwei Chen
items.summary: Abstract Achieving sustainable recycling of lithium (Li)-ion batteries requires a paradigm shift from conventional elemental recovery toward chemistry-guided regeneration of functional electrode materials. Here, we establish a coordination-mediated semisolid regeneration paradigm that directly reconstructs spent LiFePO 4 into high-performance LiMn 0.6 Fe 0.4 PO 4 . Within an oxalate-coordinated reaction field, proton-assisted lattice deconstruction is coupled with selective elemental decoupling, extracting Li while retaining Fe as a structurally defined ferrous oxalate intermediate. The recovered Li is converted into LiH 2 PO 4 , while the oxalate intermediate serves as a regulated precursor for olivine reconstruction. Subsequent thermal transformation promotes homogeneous cation redistribution, conformal carbon coating, and crystallographic re-equilibration, yielding a structurally ordered and electronically homogeneous cathode. The regenerated material delivers 156.5 mAh g –1 at 0.2 C and retains 91.2% of its initial capacity after 1000 cycles at 2 C. This work establishes semisolid regeneration as a chemistry-guided route for value-added upcycling of spent polyanionic cathodes.

items.title: Modulating Lipid Nanoparticles for Spleen Targeted RNA Delivery
authors: Kseniia Vlasova, Noorjahan Aibani, Mrinmoy Sanyal, Marco Herrera, Avisek Deyati, Pierrot Harvie, Seba Jumaa, Daniel Arriaza, Miao-Chih Tsai, Ravindra Majeti, William J. Greenleaf, Anitha Thomas, and Howard Y. Chang
items.summary: Abstract Conventional lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) efficiently deliver RNA to the liver in preclinical models, but achieving clinically relevant delivery to other tissues remains a major challenge. Here we vary ionizable lipids and stabilizers along with optimizing formulation parameters for passive targeted delivery of circular RNA without permanently charged lipids. We generated a library of 216 LNP formulations and screened them in vitro in Jurkat cells and human primary T-cells. The lead candidates were explored for their efficacy in vivo via multiple routes of administration. Our results show that optimization of the lipid ratio decreases hepatic delivery while enhancing splenic accumulation. This improved tissue tropism to the spleen induces distinct transcriptomic remodeling in vivo compared with conventional SM-102 LNPs. These findings demonstrate that extrahepatic targeting of LNPs can be achieved without altering charge of the LNPs and further reveal that hepatic detargeting efficiency could be influenced by the immune status of the recipient.

items.title: Temperature-Dependent Relaxation Pathways in Perovskite BIC Exciton-Polariton Condensation
authors: Yuexing Xia, Xin Zeng, Tongcai Yuan, Yiyang Gong, Xiaotian Bao, Shuai Yue, Jianhui Fu, Wenna Du, and Xinfeng Liu
items.summary: Abstract Exciton-polariton systems supported by bound states in the continuum (BICs) constitute an appealing platform for integrated on-chip quantum photonic devices, benefiting from their ultrahigh quality factors, enhanced light–matter coupling, and long-range spatial coherence. However, the lasing behaviors of BIC lasers under variable-temperature environments, particularly the microscopic relaxation pathways governing polariton condensate formation, remain ambiguous. Here we report a systematic investigation of temperature-driven condensation dynamics in perovskite BIC exciton-polaritons over 4–300 K, using steady-state and ultrafast spectroscopic characterizations. We identify three distinct temperature regimes governing polariton population relaxation: phonon-assisted scattering prevails above 226 K; a phonon bottleneck governs between 105 and 226 K originating from inhibited phonon-mediated relaxation; and exciton-reservoir-assisted population transfer dominates below 105 K, accompanied by anomalous line-width broadening of the polariton condensate. These results uncover the temperature-modulated relaxation physics of perovskite BIC exciton-polaritons and provide practical guidelines for optimizing polariton lasers and integrated quantum photonic hardware.

items.title: Self-Assembling Peptide Materials for the Treatment of Infectious and Biofilm-Related Diseases
authors: Christian S. Carnero Canales, Miguel D’Agostino dos Santos, Subham Kumar Vishwakarma, Cesar Augusto Roque-Borda, Rafael Miguel Sábio, Fernando Rogério Pavan, and Hélder A. Santos
items.summary: Abstract Antimicrobial peptides frequently lose efficacy in biofilms because heterogeneous extracellular matrixes restrict access to microbial cells and compromise peptide stability. Self-assembly can modify these constraints by controlling the physical state in which the peptides encounter pathogens. This review examines how molecular interactions and infection-associated signals govern supramolecular transitions and how these changes influence antimicrobial activity. A recurring challenge is balancing penetration into biofilms with sufficient retention and contact at microbial interfaces: structures that persist locally may struggle to reach deeply embedded cells, whereas more mobile assemblies may provide limited exposure. Yet, many reported improvements remain difficult to attribute specifically to self-assembly because peptide chemistry and formulation effects are not adequately controlled. Establishing clear relationships between the assembly state and biological function will require comparisons under infection-relevant conditions and should inform the design of peptide materials for persistent infections.

items.title: Au-Free Hexagonal SiGe Nanowires and Quantum Dots
authors: Denny Lamon, Marijn J. J. M. V. Hendrikx, Marvin M. Jansen-Zilles, Ries Koolen, Marcel A. Verheijen, and Erik P. A. M. Bakkers
items.summary: Abstract Ge and SiGe alloys are promising materials for next-generation optoelectronics. In their hexagonal crystal phase, they exhibit a direct bandgap, unlike their cubic counterparts, enabling efficient infrared light emission with a wavelength tunable through the Ge content. Quantum confinement has also been demonstrated in quantum wells, quantum wires, and quantum dots (QDs). However, quantum wires and QDs are typically realized in Au-catalyzed nanowires, despite the fact that Au is incompatible with CMOS technology and introduces nonradiative recombination centers that can reduce emission efficiency. In this work, we demonstrate the growth of high-quality hexagonal SiGe nanowires and QDs using Ga as a catalyst. Nanowire length and diameter were precisely controlled, while QDs with Ge concentrations up to 80% were achieved within the predicted direct-bandgap regime. This Au-free approach provides a viable route toward CMOS-compatible hexagonal SiGe nanostructures with potentially enhanced light-emission efficiency, bringing integrated group-IV light sources closer to practical realization.

items.title: Gate-tuned optical conductivity in alternately twisted silicene multilayers
authors: Jiansheng Hu, Baojin Ding, Xiang Zhong, Junmei Zhang, Yingliang Chen, Zhaoming Fu, Weibin Zhang and Xiaobo Feng
items.summary: Based on the continuum model and Kubo linear-response theory, this work systematically investigates the optical conductivity properties of alternately twisted bilayer, trilayer, and quadrilayer silicene. We uncover a distinct optoelectronic tuning scenario in which spin–orbit coupling (SOC), lattice relaxation, perpendicular electric field (Ez ⩽ 0.09 V Å−1), and twist angle (θ ⩽ 9.43°) synergistically modulate the moiré band structure, density of states, and optical conductivity. The intrinsic SOC opens a 6–8 meV mini-gap, causing a redshift of the far-infrared conductivity peak, while lattice relaxation substantially enhances the photoresponse by increasing the moiré band velocity. Remarkably, the perpendicular electric field induces a step-like variation in the interband conductivity, while a prominent Drude-type intraband response emerges in the long-wavelength limit. As the twist angle decreases, the interband peak exhibits a strong redshift that enhances the infrared response, whereas the intraband response is progressively suppressed, revealing a synergistic yet contrasting behavior between the two channels. These findings establish alternately twisted silicene multilayers as a highly tunable platform for infrared optoelectronics, offering a new route for designing adaptive photodetectors.

items.title: Conservation laws and the non-classicality of gravity
authors: Tianfeng Feng, Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral
items.summary: We analyze the closed and autonomous interaction between quantum matter and classical objects through a general effective channel for hybrid dynamics, subject to the fundamental constraint that no quantum correlations can be generated between the classical and quantum sectors from any initially separable state. We demonstrate that, within this hybrid framework, imposing an additive conserved observable strictly forbids a classical system from altering the local observable of its quantum counterpart. Applying this no-go theorem to gravity, under the assumption of such hybrid dynamics, we show that if global momentum is conserved, a classical gravitational field cannot induce momentum in a quantum system. In contrast, a quantum gravitational field naturally facilitates such back-action. Drawing upon the fundamental relationship between conservation laws and the quantum properties of objects, our analysis provides a novel perspective for interpreting existing experimental observations, such as free fall, as potential indicators of the non-classicality of gravity.

items.title: Neural network-based finite-sample transmission coefficient estimation and uncertainty quantification in satellite-to-ground CV-QKD
authors: Jiayan Shao, Lanjian Chen, Mingshan Dong, Ao Liu, Yaping Li, Zhenrong Zhang and Chen Dong
items.summary: Satellite-to-ground continuous variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) is constrained by rapidly varying free-space channels and short transmission windows, which limit the amount of data available for parameter estimation within each channel interval. Under finite-sample conditions, parameter point estimates are subject to statistical uncertainty and may even yield an overly favorable description of the true channel state, while errors in the estimated transmission coefficient directly affect the covariance matrix used in the security analysis. In this work, we investigate the finite-sample effects of transmission coefficient estimation in dynamic free-space CV-QKD. A neural network (NN) is introduced to estimate the transmission coefficient, and the Delta method is used to quantify the uncertainty in its predictions. The proposed method is compared with the standard maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) method. Confidence intervals for the transmission coefficient are constructed for different sample sizes, and the effects of the statistical uncertainties on the secret key rate are analyzed. Under the considered Gaussian-channel simulation conditions, the NN can provide a more favorable nominal lower bound on the transmission coefficient than MLE in certain sample-limited regimes, leading to a higher parameter-estimation-limited key-rate metric. This work establishes a statistical framework that connects NN-based transmission coefficient estimation and predictive uncertainty quantification with covariance matrix construction and secret key rate analysis. It provides a basis for machine learning-assisted parameter estimation in free-space CV-QKD systems operating with finite samples.

items.title: Tailorable deep eutectic solvents for sustainable lignocellulose refining: from platform design to value-added products
items.summary: Abstract Efficient utilization of renewable carbon requires lignocellulosic biorefineries that can deconstruct plant cell walls while preserving the value of cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs), constructed from programmable hydrogen-bond acceptors and donors, have emerged as tunable media for lignocellulose processing. This review discusses recent progress in the rational design of DESs for lignocellulosic biorefineries, focusing on binary, ternary, hydrated, biphasic, catalytic and biocompatible systems. By regulating acidity/basicity, polarity, hydrogen-bonding ability, viscosity, water tolerance, active sites and phase behavior, DESs can selectively disrupt lignin-carbohydrate complexes, stabilize or functionalize the components, and direct the downstream transformation of the components toward bio-based chemicals and functional polymeric materials. Component-oriented valorization routes are summarized, including cellulose-derived functional materials and platform chemicals, lignin-derived aromatics and functional polymers, and hemicellulose-derived furan chemicals. Key barriers to industrial deployment are also critically examined, including high viscosity, mass-transfer limitations, solvent loss, energy-intensive recovery, feedstock heterogeneity, incomplete mechanistic understanding and insufficient techno-economic and life-cycle assessment. Future opportunities are highlighted in artificial-intelligence-guided DESs discovery, novel membrane and electrodialysis DES-recovery technologies, DES-compatible chemo-biocatalysis and closed-loop process integration. Tailorable DESs are expected to evolve from empirical solvent systems into predictive, recyclable and product-oriented platforms for sustainable production of bio-based chemicals, materials and fuels.

items.title: Dominant role of Southeast Asian emissions in anthropogenic increases in global tropospheric ozone and southward tropical growth, 2000–2019
items.summary: Abstract Widespread increases in tropospheric ozone (O 3 ) have been reported over the past two decades, with changes in anthropogenic emissions, particularly in Asia, identified as an important driver. Here we use global model sensitivity simulations to quantify changes in global tropospheric O 3 burden and associated radiative forcing (RF) attributable to anthropogenic emission changes from 2000 to 2019, and assess the contributions from different Asian regions. Changes in anthropogenic emissions increased the global tropospheric O 3 burden by 12.0 ± 0.5 Tg and global mean RF by 0.030 ± 0.002 W m –2 under fixed 2015–2019 meteorological fields. The increase was larger during 2000–2010 than during 2010–2019 and occurred predominantly in the tropics. Southeast Asia was the largest regional contributor over 2000–2019, accounting for 5.7 ± 0.4 Tg of the simulated global tropospheric O 3 burden increase and 0.020 ± 0.002 W m –2 of RF. During 2010–2019, the increase in tropospheric O 3 burden attributable to anthropogenic emission changes was larger over 0–30°S than over 0–30°N, indicating a southward shift in the tropical response driven primarily by Southeast Asian emissions. East Asia shifted from a major positive contributor during 2000–2010 to a negative contributor during 2010–2019. These results highlight the increasing importance of anthropogenic emissions from tropical Asia in shaping the global distribution of tropospheric O 3 and its climate forcing.

items.title: A microscopic continuum model for moiré transition metal dichalcogenides
items.summary: Twisted transition metal dichalcogenides (tTMDs) have emerged as a fascinating platform for many-body phases --- displaying fractional Chern insulators and superconductivity as a function of doping. Here, we give a microscopic derivation of a continuum model which accurately describes their bandstructure across a range of twist angles with angle-independent parameters. This angle-independent description rests on retaining both the monolayer valence and conduction bands, which introduce tunnelling paths through AB-stacked regions; upon downfolding to the valence band, these paths supply a substantial twist-tunable contribution to the interlayer coupling. We show that the model is a perturbation of a chiral model with a magic angle, explaining the near-ideal quantum geometry of the moiré bands. The model further produces a strongly different orbital magnetic moment to the single-orbital theory --- predicting an anomalous Landau level slope --- and a redistribution of charge between the layers, modifying the moiré ferroelectric potential.

items.title: Magnons in solids with correlated atomic and nanoscale disorder
items.summary: Atomic defects and disorder affect both the microscopic magnon excitations and the macroscopic physical properties of real-world magnetic materials. The rationalization of this relation has hitherto remained elusive, because of the intertwined challenges of simulating with quantum accuracy atomic- and nanoscale inhomogeneities and correlations, and their effect on the magnon spectral function determining observables such as spin stiffness. Here, we introduce a theoretical and computational framework to address these challenges. First, we develop the Coupled Optimization of SpIN Environment (COSINE) algorithm for efficiently relaxing the atomic structure and magnetic configuration of a solid with defects or disorder to a local energy minimum. Then, we discuss how to efficiently obtain exchange interactions accounting for local compositional, structural, and magnetic-moment inhomogeneities. Finally, we develop a paraunitary unfolding approach for Bogoliubov bosons, which allows us to predict the magnon spectral function in materials with any magnetic order, including systems with canting and full, partial, or no magnetic-moment compensation. We showcase our approach in a representative defective ferrimagnet for generality, and then combine it with state-of-the-art spin-informed machine-learning potentials to quantitatively predict how nonuniformities in the spatial distribution of vacancy defects control blurring of effective magnon bandstructures.

items.title: Vacuum correlation measures as CFT partition functions
items.summary: We show that in any $d$-dimensional CFT, the vacuum sandwiched Rényi mutual information (SRMI) of integer order $n$ between two disjoint balls maps to a CFT partition function on a manifold of topology $\#^{n-1}(S^1 \times S^{d-1})$, with moduli fixed by the ball configuration and single-ball modular flow. At $n=2$, it is given by the thermal partition function on $S^{d-1}$, upper-bounding the von Neumann mutual information. For $n>2$, SRMI diverges at finite separation due to a hot-spot limit of the partition function. Explicit CFT evaluations agree well with density matrix computations.

items.title: Bound Entanglement with Negative Partial Transpose Exists
items.summary: We show that the Werner state $ρ= (23 I - 3\,\mathrm{SWAP})/1448$ on $\mathbb{C}^8 \otimes \mathbb{C}^8$ has a negative partial transpose and is bound entangled: no LOCC protocol can distill entanglement from any number of copies of $ρ$, and even with separable operations the fidelity of a two-qubit output with a Bell state never exceeds $(1+\sqrt{2})/4 \approx 0.604$. It follows that distillable entanglement is neither additive nor convex.

items.title: Scalable Low-Cost Laboratory Automation: A Digital Twin-Integrated Robotic Platform for Autonomous Liquid Handling (RAINBOT)
items.summary: Laboratory automation accelerates discovery, yet its adoption is constrained by the high cost, proprietary design, and limited remote supervisability of commercial liquid-handling systems. This work presents RAINBOT\textsuperscript{TM}, a low-cost, openly reproducible liquid-handling robot built by converting a consumer-grade Cartesian 3D printer (Elegoo Neptune 4 Max). The printer extruder is replaced by a precision single-channel pipette actuated through the printer's own G-code-driven X--Y--Z gantry, with plunger and tip-eject motions effected by two compact linear actuators under Python control. To make experiments transparent and remotely supervisable, a browser-based digital twin is implemented to synchronise bidirectionally with the physical platform, mirroring kinematics and pipetting states in real time and exposing remote monitoring, intervention, and an emergency stop from any web browser. As a proof of concept, RAINBOT\textsuperscript{TM} performed sequential exchanges of differently coloured aqueous solutions while an integrated colour sensor quantified the resulting mixtures; measured red, yellow, and blue (RYB) responses agreed with expected mixing behaviour to within a mean absolute error of two percentage points, validating correct execution and real-time tracking. Closing the loop, the platform is coupled to the CEID\textsuperscript{TM} (Cooperative Explorer for Inverse Design) framework, which recasts experimentation from iterative manual guessing into a goal-directed inverse-design search while keeping a human in the loop. The complete hardware costs under US\$1300, which is roughly an order of magnitude below entry-level commercial handlers, thereby establishing an accessible physical--virtual framework for self-driving laboratory automation.

items.title: The thermodynamic budget of objectivity
items.summary: An event becomes a fact when enough independent records of it exist such that no operation is possible that leaves all observers ignorant of it again. Records are physical, and creating, keeping, and destroying them have thermodynamic costs. We compute these costs exactly in a minimal broadcast model with a driven central qubit writing records into $N$ initially thermal registers, with work sources and baths at temperature $T$. The basic arguments for the operations are outlined here, with full treatment in the text. Creation of one event record at redundancy $R$ and information deficit $δ$ requires work $W \ge R\, k_\mathrm{B}T \ln 2\, (1-δ) H(\varepsilon)$, linear in redundancy at the Landauer coefficient. Recording in a basis misaligned by $θ$ with the einselecting interaction fails at a critical angle, $θ_c = 2\arcsin\sqrt{H_2^{-1}(δ)}$, beyond which objectivity is unreachable at any work, and below $θ_c$ the optimal work is a closed form in the pointer basis that minimizes the work of objectivity. Reducing objectivity is impossible at any work with access to fewer than $R - R_{\min} + 1$ records, while work protects nothing if given access. Inter-record redundancy is extractable free energy and erasing the accessed records yields a net gain of work beyond the first copy. The second law constrains the destruction of the correlation: erasing a fact from a sector an adversary controls dissipates at least the mutual information erased, but a consolidation dissipates nothing. Records in re-thermalizing media are nonequilibrium steady states, and the minimal power to maintain a record at $(R,δ)$ is the known two-state driving bound evaluated at the record-quality boundary.

items.title: Moiré-induced self-trapping in a Bose-Einstein Condensate
items.summary: The effect of moiré modulations on two-dimensional materials flattens their electronic energy bands, which enhances the effects of interactions and has been seen to give rise to several emergent electronic phases. We demonstrate this behavior with a moiré modulation extends to a quasiperiodic hopping model of interacting bosons on the honeycomb lattice. Without interactions, the velocity vanishes at a magic-angle transition, where a sharp onset of the zero-energy density of states and multifractal low-energy states appear. Including interactions, we study its interplay with quasiperiodicity by tuning the scale associated with self-trapping and diffusive wave packet dynamics. Near the magic-angle, we find that substantially weaker interactions lead to self-trapping and diffusive wavepacket dynamics, which we attribute to the vanishing moiré-induced minibandwidth. A new computational approach is presented that combines split-step time evolution with a truncated Chebyshev expansion as an efficient and general purpose approach to solving the Gross-Pitaevskii equation in the absence of translational symmetry. We discuss how our results can be explored in ultracold atom experiments using momentum space lattices or tweezer arrays.

items.title: Brightening spin- and parity-forbidden interlayer excitons through rhombohedral stacking
items.summary: Brightened symmetry-forbidden excitons can provide critical information about the electronic structure and many-body interactions in semiconductors. Recently, interlayer atomic registry has emerged as a new way to control atomically thin layered materials in both ground and excited states. Here we show that the rhombohedral stacking in a 3R-MoS_2 homobilayer can brighten two symmetry-forbidden interlayer excitons: one is a spin-unlike 1s exciton and the other is a parity-odd 2p exciton. The nature of these interlayer excitons is revealed by their gfactors as well as the hybridization patterns observed when they are tuned to resonate with intralayer excitons. Surprisingly, the hybridized 2p exciton exhibits a constructive quantum interference between the acquired transition dipoles, revealing a hidden gauge-invariant phase contrast between the constituent electronic states. Our results establish stacking control as a powerful approach for modulating quantum phases of excitons in 2D semiconductors.

items.title: Kitaev Exchange and Altermagnetism in the Double Perovskite Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$: An Ab Initio Study
items.summary: The Co$^{2+}$-based double perovskite Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ attracts attention due to its nontrivial magnetic properties. \textit{Ab initio} density functional theory calculations reveal a substantial ferromagnetic Kitaev exchange $|K|\sim J/3$ between nearest neighbors that, combined with the face-centered cubic lattice, leads to pronounced exchange frustration and places Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ among Kitaev materials with moderate Kitaev interaction strength. In addition, Sr$_2$CoTeO$_6$ is found to be altermagnetic with a sizable non-relativistic spin splitting, which can give rise to a transverse piezomagnetic effect and a nontrivial magneto-optical response.

items.title: The role of entropy production and thermodynamic uncertainty relations in the asymmetric thermalization of open quantum systems
items.summary: The asymmetry between heating and cooling in open quantum systems is a hallmark of nonequilibrium dynamics. Here, we investigate the thermalization of a quantum system weakly coupled to a bosonic thermal bath under detailed balance, focusing on the entropy production rate and the quantum thermokinetic uncertainty relation (TKUR). Within the sector of states that remain diagonal in the energy basis we derive a perturbative expression for the time-dependent entropy production rate by expanding the relative entropy around equilibrium in terms of Liouvillian eigenmodes. Through this expansion, we determine that the spectral gap, the overlap of the initial state with the slowest decay mode, and the mode weight control the entropy production. Particularly for the thermal qubit, the ratio of the initial rates of heating and cooling has an exact closed form. Heating involves a higher initial entropy production, and hence faster thermalization, solely because of its larger spectral gap, i.e., the bath-temperature dependence of the dissipative rate. The TKUR is then used as a diagnostic tool that relates the asymmetry to the precision bounds on heat-current fluctuations. The analysis presented here is intended to clarify the thermodynamic origin of the asymmetry within the well-controlled Markovian case.

items.title: Transition Path Sampling for Rare Events in Non-Markovian Open Quantum Systems
items.summary: Rare transitions govern the dynamics of many open quantum systems, but their probabilities and rates are difficult to calculate. Transition path sampling (TPS) of quantum systems has so far been limited to Markovian, perturbative descriptions. Here, we formulate TPS for non-Markovian quantum state diffusion, which is exact for Gaussian baths, extending it to non-Markovian and strongly coupled open quantum systems. For normal-to-superradiant tunneling in the unbalanced open Dicke model, we determine probabilities down to $10^{-8}$ and rates beyond the reach of brute force.

items.title: Spin Loop Currents and Bulk-Edge Structure in Correlated Topological States of WSe$_2$/MoTe$_2$ Bilayers
items.summary: Motivated by recent experiments, we theoretically investigate AB-stacked WSe$_2$/MoTe$_2$ bilayers. Our theory incorporates valence fluctuations, local and extended (longer-range) Hubbard interactions, including non-local interactions between carriers on the MoTe$_2$ layer. Within the parton mean-field framework, we show that the non-local interaction between MoTe$_2$ carriers can drive a transition between a topological Kondo semimetal(TKSM) and a topological Kondo insulator(TKI) at the filling fraction $ν=2$. We attribute this transition to an emergent spin-loop current arising from the interplay between Ising spin-orbit coupling and non-local electron correlations. In addition, we investigate how the emergent spin-loop current affects edge transport and show that the two-point conductance takes a quantized value at certain bias voltages.

items.title: Magnetic Contributions to Phase Stability in the Co-Ni Binary: A First-Principles CALPHAD Study
items.summary: We propose a simple method to employ ab-initio calculations to determine magnetic contributions to free energy of alloys. Validation on the Co-Ni binary demonstrates that this ab initio approach reproduces experimental FCC-HCP phase equilibria while providing physically transparent, structure-dependent magnetic parameters suitable for multicomponent extrapolation. Our results demonstrate that physically grounded magnetic parametrization, derived directly from electronic structure calculations, enables predictive phase diagram modeling for magnetic alloy systems.

items.title: Monotonic probes of asymmetry and robustness of the quantum Mpemba effect
items.summary: Entanglement asymmetry has emerged as a powerful probe of symmetry restoration and the quantum Mpemba effect. However, its conventional Rényi generalizations, defined as differences of Rényi entropies, are not monotones in the resource-theoretic sense. Here, we investigate an alternative family of asymmetry quantifiers based on sandwiched Rényi divergences, which satisfy monotonicity under symmetry-preserving quantum channels. Developing a two-parameter replica approach, we show how these quantities can be computed from charged moments and establish a remarkable correspondence with conventional Rényi asymmetries under the inversion of the Rényi index, $α\leftrightarrow 1/α$. This relation, exact for pure states, holds at leading order in the relevant scaling limits for homogeneous quantum quenches, including interacting integrable systems, and for Haar-random states. Applying these results to quenches from tilted ferromagnetic states, we demonstrate that the quantum Mpemba effect is remarkably robust, occurring throughout the entire family of sandwiched Rényi asymmetry monotones. We identify dynamical regimes in quenches from spatially inhomogeneous initial states where conventional Rényi asymmetries and genuine monotones exhibit qualitatively different behaviours. We also investigate a solvable toy model illustrating the possible dependence of Mpemba crossings on the Rényi index. Our findings establish a connection between conventional Rényi asymmetries and quantum resource theory, explaining their effectiveness in broad classes of nonequilibrium protocols while highlighting the additional information provided by genuine asymmetry monotones.

items.title: Measuring a buried Bi$_2$Te$_3$ epitaxial film through a protective Te cap: an exact three-layer terahertz analysis
items.summary: Air-sensitive chalcogenide films are routinely protected by a capping layer, which must then be removed, or contacted through, before electronic transport can be measured, destroying the surface the cap was meant to preserve. Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy requires neither, but using it quantitatively demands a transmission model in which cap, film and substrate are treated on an equal footing. We formulate the cap/film/substrate problem exactly using a transfer matrix with a time-gated substrate, and show that the intuitive construction in which each thin layer contributes an independent Fabry--Pérot factor fails for two adjacent thin films. In the thin-film limit we obtain a closed-form inversion together with a criterion for the error incurred by ignoring the cap. We apply the framework to Bi$_2$Te$_3$ films grown by molecular beam epitaxy on GaAs at three thicknesses, each prepared with and without a 25 nm Te cap. A Te-on-GaAs witness shows the cap to be optically indistinguishable from bare substrate, transmitting 1.00(4) of the substrate amplitude between 0.2 and 1.5 THz, which limits the error from neglecting it to 3.6 % for the 90 nm film, although the same estimate reaches 48 % at 25 nm. In this matched set, the capped films form an ordered series, monotonic in thickness in both conductance magnitude and lineshape, whereas the uncapped films do not. The capping layer therefore presents no obstacle to terahertz characterization, and in this set it coincides with a more reproducible film response.

items.title: AlphaDiffract: Automated Crystallographic Analysis of Powder X-ray Diffraction Data
items.summary: Materials identification and structural understanding from powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) data are long-standing challenges in materials science, fundamental to discovering and characterizing novel materials. A prerequisite for full structure solution is the accurate determination of the crystal lattice, including lattice parameters and crystallographic symmetries. Traditional methods for this are iterative and typically require expert input, and while existing deep learning approaches have shown promise, a robust, single-shot method for comprehensive lattice determination from experimental data remains a key goal. Here, we introduce AlphaDiffract, a deep learning framework for jointly predicting the crystal system, space group, and lattice parameters directly from PXRD patterns. AlphaDiffract utilizes a 1D adaptation of the ConvNeXt architecture, a modern convolutional neural network that integrates key design principles from transformers, coupled with dedicated prediction heads for each crystallographic property. The model is trained and validated on the largest-to-date physics-based dataset of over 31 million simulated diffraction patterns, generated by augmenting 312,267 curated structures from the ICSD and Materials Project databases. Crucially, it demonstrates strong transfer from simulated training data to experimental measurements, achieving 81.7% crystal system accuracy and 66.2% space group accuracy on the RRUFF dataset while additionally predicting all six lattice parameters. By providing a unified model for rapid, simultaneous prediction of lattice symmetry and parameters from PXRD data, AlphaDiffract represents a significant step forward in leveraging deep learning for high-throughput materials discovery.

items.title: Localization of an Individual Charge Fluctuator in a Si/SiGe Spin Qubit Device
items.summary: Charge noise from two-level fluctuators (TLFs) limits gate fidelities in semiconductor spin qubits, yet locating individual fluctuators within a device remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a spatial triangulation method that combines the gate dependence of a TLF's detuning with the chemical potential shifts it induces in a sensing dot. Applying this method to previously reported measurements from a gated Si/SiGe quantum dot device, we use electrostatic simulations to jointly constrain the fluctuator's three-dimensional position and the magnitude of its electric dipole moment. We localize the fluctuator to a region spanning 31 nm by 1 nm laterally and 4 nm vertically within the bulk of the atomic layer deposited aluminum oxide, identifying the material hosting this individual charge-noise source. The measurements are consistent with a vertically oriented TLF with a magnitude of 3 to 4 e$\mathring{A}$. This approach provides a route to determining which materials and interfaces host active charge fluctuators in semiconductor spin qubit devices.

items.title: Discotic columnar phase in a three-dimensional monomer-tetramer model of Heilmann and Lieb with side-to-side attraction
items.summary: We study Model III of Heilmann--Lieb (1979), a lattice model for liquid crystals consisting of tetramers (plaquettes) on the cubic lattice at chemical potential $μ$, interacting via a hard-core repulsion and a lateral attraction of strength $a>0$ between coplanar, aligned tetramers. The model was conjectured to exhibit liquid-crystalline order at low temperature provided that $μ+2a>0$. We establish discotic columnar order throughout this regime, fully resolving the conjecture. Specifically, we prove the existence of exactly twelve extremal and periodic Gibbs measures, each breaking rotational symmetry, with one of three tetramer orientations dominant, and translational symmetry in exactly two directions, with one of four tetramer parities dominant within that orientation. Thus, the tetramers form one-dimensional columns arranged on a square lattice. This arrangement is not a priori evident from the zero-temperature picture, where energy only enforces a layered structure: each layer is fully packed and crystalline, but different layers are free to shift independently within their planes. The main novelty here lies in showing how thermal fluctuations lift this degeneracy in favor of the twelve ground states in which all tetramers share a common parity.

items.title: Realizing Braided Fusion 2-Categories as (3+1)D Mixed-State Topological Orders
items.summary: We construct large families of mixed-state topological orders in (3+1)D, including intrinsically mixed-state topological orders. We realize these theories by relating the data parameterizing braided fusion 2-categories to the strong higher-form symmetries and their anomalies that characterize mixed-state topological order. We focus here on bosonic theories, which include theories which admit an emergent fermion in the spectrum of line operators. Our general framework is exemplified on the lattice, where we present concrete models and identify how the data of braided fusion 2-categories are physically encoded. We then formalize this data and show that every braided fusion 2-category arises from a general construction (decoherence followed by strong and weak gauging) as the category of topological operators of a (3+1)D mixed state, with intrinsically mixed-state topological orders distinguished by the presence of strong higher-form symmetries whose anomalies cannot be realized in any (3+1)D gapped ground state. Notably, we show that (3+1)D admits a new mechanism with no (2+1)D counterpart: intrinsically mixed-state order whose topological operators braid non-degenerately, but which carries a gravitational anomaly.

items.title: Emergent Chern metal in strongly correlated moiré bilayers
items.summary: We investigate the topological properties of a strongly correlated moiré transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) bilayer (such as twisted $\mathrm{MoTe}_2$ or $\mathrm{WSe}_2$) hosting a spin-charge separated state coupled to a layer-polarized helical spin texture. Analyzing an effective low-energy Hamiltonian for mobile spinless holons moving through this non-coplanar spinon background, we reveal pronounced asymmetric band warping. This warping closes the global indirect band gap across most of the parameter space, restricting true topological insulators to fine-tuned critical trajectories. However, a finite local direct gap persists, stabilizing broad regions of a topological Chern metal ($C = \pm 1$). Computing the Chern number and density of states, we demonstrate that this phase naturally yields a sizable, non-quantized anomalous Hall response accompanied by finite longitudinal conduction, providing a purely electronic strong-coupling mechanism for dissipative anomalous Hall states in moiré systems.

items.title: Stability and superstructural ordering of alkali-triel-pnictide clathrates A$_8$T$_{27}$Pn$_{19}$
items.summary: Clathrates are a class of inclusion compounds that offer various useful and surprising phenomena, including superconductivity, thermoelectricity, and the potential for high-density ion storage. Stability conditions within the Alkali-Triel-Pnictide A$_8$T$_{27}$Pn$_{19}$ family of unconventional clathrates are investigated with high-throughput density functional theory calculations, establishing trends in formation energy, structural and electronic properties, and identifying several new potential candidates. Electronic structure calculations and first-principles molecular dynamics simulations show that all alkali guests are fully ionized in the framework, and that the stability of electron-exact clathrates correlates with the ionization potential of the guest atoms, while their rattling behavior is governed primarily by the size of the guest ions relative to the cages. Targeted reactive synthesis from elemental precursors is attempted, resulting in four previously unreported ternary phases, two of which are structurally characterized. However, the predicted clathrate phases are not obtained. Further analysis reveals that the stability of ATPn clathrate compounds containing heavy elements, such as bismuth, depends strongly on relativistic spin-orbit coupling, which is often neglected in high-throughput studies that compute formation energies. Finally, chemically induced superstructural ordering is described in relation to Wyckoff sites in the prototypical type-I clathrate unit cell.

items.title: Dynamical Complexity of Projected Ensembles: A Geometric Quantum State Approach
items.summary: We study the emergence of complexity in finite-size quantum systems as their dynamics transition from closed and coherent evolution to interacting and effectively open behavior. Using a state-based geometric framework, we represent mixed quantum states as probability measures on complex projective Hilbert space. Obtained by conditioning on the environment in a fixed basis, these geometric quantum states coincide with the projected ensembles that underlie deep thermalization and emergent quantum state designs. This representation allows us to track how interactions reshape the underlying pure-state geometry. We introduce two complementary diagnostics, a distinguishability measure based on the Wasserstein distance between nearby projected ensembles, which quantifies sensitivity to initial states, and a state-space coverage index, which measures long-time exploration of the subsystem state space. Applied to the quantum kicked top, both diagnostics generally increase with interaction strength. Their dependence on environment size is structured by parity symmetry, with integer-spin systems often exhibiting greater sensitivity and state-space coverage than half-integer-spin systems. These results highlight finite-size quantum effects and provide a geometric approach to quantifying dynamical complexity deep in the quantum regime.

items.title: Rényi multi-entropy from Riemann surfaces
items.summary: We compute vacuum tripartite Rényi multi-entropy in a two-dimensional compact-boson conformal field theory (CFT). For every integer Rényi index $n\geq2$, we evaluate the partition function on the replica Riemann surface for disjoint intervals, obtaining the twist four-point function in terms of a ratio of theta functions. An independent calculation of the partition function on a Fermat curve yields the adjacent three-point coefficient. In the fusion limit, the Riemann surface for disjoint intervals degenerates into two Fermat curves, and the residue of the four-point function reproduces the squared three-point coefficient, as required by the operator product expansion. The genuine multi-entropy therefore approaches twice its strictly adjacent value. The CFT predictions agree with lattice calculations for the critical XXZ and Ising spin chains and a harmonic chain. We also exhibit a unitary CFT in which the canonical replica construction yields complex Rényi multi-entropy.

items.title: From Spin Glass Theory to Optimization in High Dimensions and Modern Artificial Neural Networks
items.summary: This chapter pays tribute to Giorgio Parisi by reviewing the influence of his work on spin glasses and replica symmetry breaking (RSB) on combinatorial optimization and artificial neural networks. We first introduce replica and cavity methods through the matching and traveling salesman problems, before discussing random satisfiability and the development of survey propagation. We then examine applications to neural networks, emphasizing the connections between the geometry of solution spaces, computational hardness, and learning. Particular attention is given to rare regions of high local entropy and their role in algorithmic accessibility. Examples involving overparameterized models and asymmetric recurrent networks illustrate how these ideas connect constrained optimization and inference with concepts developed in spin-glass theory.

items.title: Slow mixing of Gibbs sampling for the quantum Curie-Weiss model
items.summary: Hamiltonian evolution can spread local operators across a dense quantum magnet. We show that this global support does not remove the bottleneck to thermalization in the quantum Curie-Weiss model: at fixed low temperature and weak transverse field, the Chen-Kastoryano-Gilyen Gibbs sampler [arXiv: 2311.09207] has an exponentially large mixing-time lower bound. A dynamical quantum bottleneck theory that generalizes the classical notion of conductance has been proposed alongside existing frameworks that rely on spatial locality. We also give a complementary interpretation of slow mixing using an effective Fokker-Planck equation.

items.title: Transverse Shifts Driven by Geometric Orbital Torque in Altermagnets
items.summary: Anomalous transverse shifts in interface reflection are conventionally attributed to spin-orbit coupling or its pseudospin analogue. Here, we uncover a distinct geometric mechanism driven solely by an orbital torque arising from Fermi-surface anisotropy. During total reflection, an incident wave packet penetrates the anisotropic transmitted medium as an evanescent wave. There, the broken rotational symmetry about the interface normal exerts an orbital torque, and the accumulated angular impulse---the product of the torque and the dwell time---leads to a transverse spatial shift. Applying this mechanism to altermagnets without spin-orbit coupling, we show that the orbital torque is odd in spin. As a consequence, the two spin channels are deflected to opposite sides of the incident plane, giving an intrinsic spatial spin separation in altermagnets. The shift also inherits the angular symmetry of the altermagnetic spin splitting and is strongly enhanced near the onset of total reflection. Our work thus uncovers a new mechanism for transverse shifts, predicts a novel spin separation effect in altermagnets, and offers a direct probe of the altermagnetic order.

items.title: Probing the wave-vector gap in nanoscale magnonics
items.summary: Short-wavelength spin waves are central to miniaturizing magnonic devices and to studying exchange-dominated magnetization dynamics. Yet the wave-vector range between roughly 30 and 300 radians per micrometre has remained difficult to access experimentally, posing challenges for both excitation and detection. This Perspective reviews recent advances in emerging measurement techniques and discusses prospects for their future development. Optical and microwave techniques are restricted to the vicinity of the Brillouin-zone centre. Inelastic neutron, electron and resonant hard x-ray scattering cover the full Brillouin zone but lack the energy resolution needed for low-frequency magnons at intermediate wave vectors. This Perspective examines five emerging approaches that are beginning to close this gap: Mie-enhanced Brillouin light scattering, colour-centre magnetometry, magnon momentum microscopy, extreme-ultraviolet transient-grating spectroscopy, and time-resolved scanning transmission x-ray microscopy. For each, we discuss the physical principle, demonstrated capabilities, current limitations and prospects for development. Compared side by side, the techniques give complementary access to magnon frequencies, local stray fields, real-space dynamics and momentum-space distributions, and they differ in their sensitivity to coherent and incoherent excitations. We therefore discuss the main advantages and use cases of each technique and consider the practical requirements for addressing different scientific questions. We highlight opportunities for further development, including higher sensitivity, improved spatial and temporal resolution, and broader frequency and wave-vector coverage. Together, these advances could enable, for example, systematic studies of nonlinear magnon interactions at nanoscale wavelengths and investigations of emerging magnetic materials such as altermagnets.

items.title: A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin defect emission and quantum sensing
items.summary: Spin defects in two-dimensional materials are promising platforms for quantum information technologies and nanoscale sensing. The negatively charged boron vacancy (VB-) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is particularly attractive due to its sensitivity to temperature, magnetic fields, and pressure, but its application is limited by intrinsically weak photoluminescence (PL). Here we demonstrate a van der Waals heterostructure that enhances the PL intensity of VB- by up to 45x at 4 Kelvin while preserving compatibility with ultrathin optoelectronic platforms. A type-I band alignment at the PbI2-hBN interface facilitates efficient interlayer coupling to the defect, and strong spectral overlap supports fluorescence resonance energy transfer. Ab initio calculations indicate that this coupling enables a photon-ratcheting mechanism, in which optical absorption in PbI2 generates a nonlinear polarization that drives VB- excitation. This process is consistent with interlayer energy transfer while maintaining minimal electronic and spin hybridization and preserving optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast. The heterostructure further exhibits improved sensitivity to external magnetic fields. These results establish a route for the enhancement of defect emission via interlayer optical coupling and introduce a general materials strategy for amplifying weak quantum defect signals in nanomaterials.

items.title: Frozen Phonons on Dense $\mathbf{q}$-Grids Using Set Covers
items.summary: Phonon dynamics determine a vast number of properties in the solid state, such as the heat capacity, thermal expansion, and thermal conductivity. Phonons are obtained through the dynamical matrix, which, in the frozen phonon approach, is calculated as a finite difference derivative of the analytical Hellmann-Feynman force. This approach unfortunately typically suffers from requiring very large supercells, even for modest $\mathbf{q}$-grids. The non-diagonal supercell method remedies this issue by determining the smallest supercell commensurate with a given $\mathbf{q}$-point, drastically reducing the supercell size, but in turn requiring a new supercell for each $\mathbf{q}$-point on the grid. This introduces redundancy, however, since a single non-diagonal supercell may be commensurate with several $\mathbf{q}$-points. In this work I present a method to determine a minimal set of supercells, such that every $\mathbf{q}$-point on the grid is commensurate with at least one supercell. I present an algorithm to solve the problem and prove that it yields the optimal solution, before summarizing the algorithm using pseudocode. The scaling of the number of supercells with the density of the grid is discussed. Numerical results on a variety of systems show the significant computational advantage of the method, which increases with the density of the grid.

items.title: Data-enhanced self-learning projective quantum Monte Carlo with Rydberg-atom measurements
items.summary: We introduce a data-enhanced self-learning projective quantum Monte Carlo (PQMC) method that incorporates projective measurements from programmable quantum simulators into the guiding wavefunction of a ground-state projection. We demonstrate the approach for a two-dimensional Rydberg-atom array using restricted Boltzmann machine (RBM) and recurrent neural network (RNN) guiding wavefunctions. Experimental pretraining reduces finite-population effects and accelerates self-learning convergence, allowing unbiased estimation of ground-state properties to be obtained with fewer walkers and fewer self-learning iterations. The improvement is particularly pronounced for the RBM, while the more accurate RNN guiding wavefunction exhibits a smaller, though still observable, benefit from pretraining. Simulations across different system sizes suggest that the relative advantage of experimental pretraining may increase with system size. Improvements are also observed for the checkerboard order parameter, despite deviations of the experimental measurements from the equilibrium numerical results. Finally, finite-size scaling with self-learning PQMC without experimental pretraining yields the critical point and critical exponents of the disordered-to-checkerboard transition in agreement with previous numerical studies. Our results show that limited and imperfect experimental measurements can provide an effective initialization for self-learning PQMC, while imaginary-time projection combined with subsequent unsupervised learning progressively refines the guiding wavefunction toward the ground state.

items.title: Morphogenic necking of surfaces
items.summary: Surface morphogenesis occurs across biological scales, from subcellular vesicles and cells to visceral organs, tissue organoids, and whole organisms. Since morphogenesis often involves changes in topology, a natural question is that of appropriate mathematical descriptions that provide an approach to topological transitions of thin surfaces. Here, we suggest a general intrinsic framework coupling morphogen organization to surface geometry. We propose a minimal geometric model in which smoothing competes with morphogen-induced deformation to regulate shape, while loss of this balance can bring a surface toward a topological transition via neck constriction. A simple dynamical model coupling a scalar field to the surface metric reveals two mechanisms: gradient-driven constriction at steep morphogen transitions and curvature-driven constriction near localized morphogen peaks. For frozen morphogen profiles in simple axisymmetric examples, the gradient-driven route gives exact algebraic contraction, while the curvature-driven route gives local exponential contraction.

items.title: Genuine multientropy, dihedral invariants and Lifshitz theory
items.summary: Multi-invariants are local-unitary invariants of state replicas introduced as potential probes of multipartite entanglement and correlations in quantum many-body systems. In this paper, we investigate two multi-invariants for tripartite pure states, namely multientropy and dihedral invariant. We compute the (genuine) multientropy for Lifshitz groundstates, and obtain its analytical continuation to noninteger values of Rényi index. We show that the genuine multientropy can be expressed in terms of mutual information and logarithmic negativity, a relation that also holds for stabilizer states. For general tripartite pure states, we demonstrate that dihedral invariants are related to Rényi reflected entropies. In particular, we show that the dihedral permutations of replicas are equivalent to the reflected construction, or alternatively to the realignment of density matrices.

items.title: The flux of particles in a one-dimensional Fleming-Viot process
items.summary: The Fleming-Viot process describes a system of $N$ particles diffusing on a graph with an absorbing site. Whenever one of the particles is absorbed, it is replaced by a new particle at the position of one of the $N-1$ remaining particles. Here we consider the case where the particles lie on the semi-infinite line with a biased diffusion towards the origin which is the absorbing site. In the large $N$ limit, the evolution of the density becomes deterministic and has a number of characteristics similar to the Fisher-KPP equation: a one-parameter family of steady state solutions, dependence of the long time asymptotics on the initial conditions, Bramson logarithmic shift, etc. One noticeable difference, however, is that in the Fleming-Viot case, the solution can be computed explicitly for arbitrary initial conditions and at an arbitrary time. By modifying the diffusion rule near the origin, one can produce a transition in the flux of absorbed particles, very similar to the pushed-pulled transition in travelling waves. Lastly, when a cut-off of order $1/N$ is added to the hydrodynamic equation, we find corrections of order $(\ln N)^{-2}$ or $N^{-γ}$ to the flux of absorbed particles, depending on whether the front is pulled or pushed, as for the correction to the velocity in travelling waves.

items.title: Reflected entropy and Markov gap in Lifshitz theories
items.summary: We study the reflected entropy in $(1+1)$--dimensional Lifshitz field theory whose groundstate is described by a quantum mechanical model. Starting from tripartite Lifshitz groundstates, both critical and gapped, we derive explicit formulas for the Rényi reflected entropies reduced to two adjacent or disjoint intervals, directly in the continuum. We show that the reflected entropy in Lifshitz theory does not satisfy monotonicity, in contrast to what is observed for free relativistic fields. We analytically compute the full reflected entanglement spectrum for two disjoint intervals, finding a discrete set of eigenvalues which is that of a thermal density matrix. Furthermore, we investigate the Markov gap, defined as the difference between reflected entropy and mutual information, and find it to be universal and nonvanishing, signaling irreducible tripartite entanglement in Lifshitz groundstates. We also obtain analytical results for the reflected entropies and the Markov gap in $2 + 1$ dimensions. Finally, as a byproduct of our results on reflected entropy, we provide exact formulas for two other entanglement-related quantities, namely the computable cross-norm negativity and the operator entanglement entropy.

items.title: Tripartite entanglement dynamics following a quantum quench
items.summary: We investigate the dynamics of multipartite entanglement after quenches from initial states which generate multiplets of quasiparticle excitations beyond the usual pair structure. We focus on the dynamics of tripartite entanglement through the lens of the Markov gap -- a computable quantity that signals irreducible tripartite entanglement when positive. In the tight-binding chain, we show that the Markov gap is positive at intermediate times, implying the presence of tripartite entanglement. After a time delay, the Markov gap increases and then decays at longer times, thus exhibiting an entanglement barrier. We argue that those qualitative features are consistent with an interpretation of the spreading of tripartite entanglement by triplets of tripartite-entangled quasiparticles.

items.title: Inferring Experimental Objectives in Microscopy Experiments from Decision Traces
items.summary: Modern microscopes can acquire, analyze and act on data far faster than human operators can decide what to measure next. Exploiting this speed in automated experiments requires the instrument to follow the scientific logic of the operator, and one way to encode that logic is through reward functions that become part of the operation process. Here we explore whether such reward functions can be learned from the decision histories of microscope operators. We propose multiple frameworks in which recorded choices among alternative measurement locations serve as comparative evidence about the operator's preferences, and we compare several algorithms for reconstructing the reward including interpretable linear models built on physically meaningful image descriptors, nonlinear functions of the same descriptors, an unsupervised image representation followed by preference modeling, and a preference trained deep kernel inspired model. The result of this analysis is a spatial field of reward functions over the sample that can be used to run the instrument. We also propose a way to benchmark these approaches, based on withheld decisions and on decision histories generated with known objectives. We then examine the possibility that a decision history contains changing priorities throughout the experiment. A hidden Markov model assigns distinct rewards to recurring selection strategies, whereas a continuous-state model tracks smoothly varying preference weights. Controlled sequences generated over real microscopy candidate sets show that both concealed switches and gradual drift can be recovered. These reward functions, learned directly from recorded decisions, provide candidate objectives for future automated microscopy experiments.

items.title: Origin of the anomalous shape of the $γ$-loop in paramagnetic Fe1-xCrx alloys from coupled Atomistic Spin Dynamics and ab initio Molecular Dynamics
items.summary: The region of fcc stability in Fe-rich Fe-Cr alloys, the $γ$-loop, has an anomalous shape: at low temperatures, Cr addition initially stabilizes fcc, but above 8 at.% Cr it stabilizes bcc. At high temperatures, Cr always stabilizes bcc. This behavior reflects a delicate balance between magnetic, vibrational and configurational free-energy contributions that is challenging to capture from first principles. We investigate phase stability in Fe1-xCrx (x = 0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15) using coupled atomistic spin dynamics and ab initio molecular dynamics with thermodynamic integration. Gibbs free energy differences between fcc and bcc are calculated from 800 to 1800 K. Our calculations reproduce the experimental $γ$-loop and its compositional dependence, with near-quantitative accuracy for the $γ$-$δ$ transition. The $α$-$γ$ boundary, including its anomalous shape, is reproduced qualitatively, although transition temperatures are underestimated by approximately 200 K. Static calculations of magnetically ordered and disordered states provide an explanation: in ordered states, increasing Cr initially reduces the energetic preference for bcc over fcc, whereas in disordered states, Cr progressively stabilizes bcc at all compositions. Vibrational effects contribute to phase stability, while atomic short-range clustering at higher Cr content ($x \geq 0.15$) may explain the observed closing of the $γ$-loop from below. The simulations reveal finite Cr moments in the paramagnetic state, whose magnitudes depend on their local magnetic environment. The results demonstrate that the anomalous $γ$-loop arises from the interplay of magnetic energetics, magnetic disorder, lattice vibrations and chemical clustering, which must be treated on equal footing to capture phase stability from first principle

items.title: Measuring the Roughness of Quasi-Circular Interfaces at Finite Resolution
items.summary: Interface roughness characterizes the boundary fluctuations across different length scales, which can reveal information about a material''s pinning landscape and collective interfacial behaviour. Finite sampling and image resolution can bias the measured scaling properties, however. These effects can particularly complicate comparisons between circular domains of different sizes, where the number of resolved boundary points, and the relationship between angular and physical separations vary with the interface radius. Here, we benchmark the recovery of the roughness exponent and amplitude using synthetic self-affine interfaces generated by Fourier synthesis, mapped onto circular contours, and rasterized onto a pixel grid. We first compare displacement-correlation (B(r)) and structure-factor (S(q)) estimates for different interface lengths. To address non-uniform angular and radial spacing in a circular interface, we assess a reconstruction procedure that weights slope minimization against medial interface position. We find that while spectral estimates were most effective in the original interfaces, this advantage did not persist after circular mapping. Moderate smoothing was found to improve parameter recovery, but stronger smoothing can bias both the scaling exponent and roughness amplitude. These results, verified on both synthetic datasets, and an experimental ferroelectric system, identify limitations of circular-interface roughness measurements and provide a basis for further investigations into the evolution of circular domains under finite resolution experiments.

items.title: Distribution of the ratio of the two smallest eigenphases of the Jacobi unitary ensemble
items.summary: We compute the joint distribution of the two smallest eigenvalues of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and the distribution of their ratio. We use a framework for calculating Janossy densities based on the Tracy-Widom system of ordinary differential equations. For the cases studied here, the leading finite-N correction to the ratio distribution, relative to its universal Bessel-kernel limit, is O(N^{-4}). This behaviour reflects a nontrivial cancellation of lower-order corrections present in the Jacobi kernel. Eigenphase ratios may thus reveal subtle finite-size effects in quantum-chaotic systems with particle-hole or chiral symmetry. As an exploratory arithmetic application, we compare the ratio distribution for the two lowest zeros of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions with the hard-edge limit for Sp(N). The data indicate that the N_{eff}^{-1} term vanishes, leaving an O(N_{eff}^{-2}) correction.

items.title: Arbitrarily Weak Losses Destroy Fractal Bandstructure in Temporal Fibonacci Quasicrystals
items.summary: Lossless photonic crystals with weak refractive index contrasts block limited frequencies. However, the same materials arranged in a non-periodic Fibonacci quasicrystal block all but infinitely rare fractally-distributed frequencies. Similar analysis shows that weak quasiperiodic refractive index variation in time should achieve infinitely broadband gain. We demonstrate that any small experimental losses immediately destroy this effect. Our methods also provide smoothness and approximation theorems for the localisation lengths central to topology in spatial problems.

items.title: EGQCA Code: automated high-throughput thermodynamic modeling of solid solutions
items.summary: Modeling disordered systems from first principles across the full composition range is a long-standing computational challenge. We present a code package implementing the extended generalized quasichemical approximation (EGQCA), which describes solid solutions through the statistics of a finite set of clusters and enables their thermodynamic modeling at arbitrary compositions and temperatures. The package automates the complete workflow and interfaces with both DFT codes and universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs). We show that replacing DFT with uMLIPs reduces the cost of the cluster calculations by up to five orders of magnitude while preserving the thermodynamic predictions. To make computationally demanding properties tractable, we additionally introduce a cluster-selection algorithm that identifies the most relevant configurations. Together, these developments establish EGQCA as a fast and accurate framework for the thermodynamic modeling of solid solutions and a practical route toward high-throughput screening of disordered materials.

items.title: SCO-Hyper-Meta-Double-GroupNN: A Double-Group SU(2) Hyper-/Meta-Graph Neural Network for Cooperative Spin-Crossover Potential Energy Surfaces
items.summary: Learning potential energy surfaces for magnetic materials requires resolving coupled local spin manifolds and geometric frustration. We introduce SCO-Hyper-Meta-Double-GroupNN, a geometry-only architecture combining a pretrained O(3)-equivariant backbone with SU(2) spinor Hamiltonians and cooperative hyper-/meta-graph interactions. Analytic thermal spinor density matrices provide non-polynomial two- and three-body structural invariants, while frustrated-triangle hyperedges and a multi-shell sideway gate couple geometric representations to local spin manifolds. A variationally consistent, doubly-centered zero-gauge free-energy functional couples multiplet occupations and signed spin orientations, yielding conservative autograd forces without spin inputs at inference. On a first-principles Co-Cr-Ni benchmark comprising 346 training and 59 held-out validation supercells across crystalline, amorphous, glassy, and liquid regimes, compact models with 56k-77k parameters outperform a 207k-parameter spin-conditioned magnetic MACE baseline. Energy MAE decreases by 37-44%, reaching 3.82 versus 6.83 meV/atom, and force MAE decreases by 10.8-14.2 meV/Angstrom, reaching 165.8-169.2 versus 180.0 meV/Angstrom. The models preserve Kramers degeneracy to within $6\times10^{-15}$ eV, predict equilibrium local magnetic moments from geometry alone with an absolute-moment MAE of $0.181\,μ_B$, and support stable molecular dynamics up to 2,200 K. This framework integrates local spinor symmetry and cooperative magnetic interactions into geometry-only interatomic potentials.

items.title: High-Throughput Orientation Extraction via Symmetry-Adapted Filters
items.summary: An algorithm for finding the orientation of objects in an image that have a known rotational symmetry, the symmetry-adapted filter (SAF) algorithm, is presented. It is deterministic and training-free, which makes it fast and reproducible. A filter that encodes the known rotational symmetry and approximate peak width is centered on the symmetry center of the object of interest, masked to the region of interest, and rotated to maximize its inner product with the image. The approach is demonstrated on more than 20,000 small-angle neutron scattering images of a torque-driven skyrmion lattice. It is also demonstrated on atomically resolved real-space images, where mapping local atomic orientations enabled the identification of grains and grain boundaries and the quantification of lattice relaxation.

items.title: Diffusion Effects on a Stochastic Amplifier Driven by the Square of a Gaussian Field: Discontinuous Transition to Intermittency
items.summary: We study the effects of diffusion on the transition to intermittency in stochastic amplification driven by the square of a Gaussian field. The transition is characterized by an order parameter quantifying the spatial uniformity of the amplification. We consider a model in which the diffusion-amplification process is embedded in a random lattice of point absorbers in such a way that the Feynman-Kac formula is restricted to Brownian paths with a range not exceeding a finite cut-off. In this setting, with the Gaussian driving field in a wide class of physical interest, we show that diffusion-induced damping of the amplification is sufficiently strong to change the nature of the transition: from continuous in the absence of diffusion, to discontinuous in the presence of diffusion.

items.title: Many-Anyon Braiding in Non-Abelian Fractional Quantum Hall Effect with Hybrid Monte Carlo Simulation
items.summary: We use the hybrid Monte Carlo method to efficiently compute the many-anyon non-Abelian braiding matrices for different Moore-Read quasiholes braiding schemes. Using both a traditional two-anyon braiding scheme and a newly proposed braiding scheme based on global rotation, we approximate the non-Abelian characteristic length of Moore-Read quasiholes around $2.8$ times the magnetic length. We also apply this method to braiding schemes involving six anyons and explicitly show that the well-known ``even-odd effect'' can be flipped by tuning electrostatic potentials. This phenomenon emphasizes the importance of accounting for all anyons within a non-Abelian system, even if the braiding involves only several anyons locally. Our results are relevant to the experimental realization of non-Abelian physics in fractional quantum Hall and other analogous systems, including the fast-growing field of fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in moiré materials.

items.title: Two-dimensional stealthy hyperuniform polycrystalline disk packings
items.summary: Polycrystals consist of grains of local crystalline order separated by grain boundaries. Conventional polycrystals are generally not hyperuniform because their randomly sized and oriented grains sustain long-wavelength density fluctuations. We use collective-coordinate optimization to generate ultradense, two-dimensional polycrystalline packings of identical disks that are stealthy hyperuniform (SHU): their structure factor vanishes over a finite range of wave numbers around the origin. We compare them with nonhyperuniform polycrystalline disk packings generated by a modified Lubachevsky-Stillinger (LS) rapid compression algorithm, a molecular dynamics protocol that models conventional polycrystalline microstructures. We compare two-point statistics, grain-size distributions, specific surface area, diffusion spreadability, and the imaginary part of the effective dynamic dielectric constant. At high packing fractions, the grain-size distribution of SHU polycrystals exhibits a peak at a characteristic size, reflecting long-range correlations between grains. This peak is absent in LS polycrystals. SHU packings also exhibit enhanced long-time diffusion spreadability. Within the nonlocal strong-contrast expansion, dielectric SHU packings are perfectly transparent to electromagnetic waves at small wave numbers, whereas LS packings retain finite attenuation. Although SHU polycrystals are not generally expected to form spontaneously, long-range interactions or correlated substrates may provide routes to their formation. They can also be fabricated as metamaterials by nanolithography or 3D printing.

items.title: Machine-Learning-Enhanced Mapping of Activity and Selectivity in CO$_2$ Hydrogenation across Metal-Alloy Surfaces
items.summary: Adsorption energy distributions (AEDs) have emerged as a powerful and increasingly adopted descriptor for catalytic performance in high-entropy alloys and, more recently, in conventional metallic alloy nanocrystal catalysts. By accounting for diverse adsorption sites and crystallographic facets, AEDs more fully represent nanoparticle-based catalytic surfaces and show strong promise for accelerating rational design and discovery of heterogeneous catalysts, especially for CO$_2$ hydrogenation. However, previous high-throughput screenings have not provided simultaneous facet-level insight into catalytic activity, product selectivity, and thermodynamic stability. Here, we implement and extend the AED framework to individual crystallographic facets, combining facet-resolved adsorption fingerprints with Wulff-derived facet abundances and an interpretable latent-space analysis of C1-product selectivity. We employ universal machine-learned force fields trained on Open Catalyst data to compute adsorption energies across 226 experimentally observed metals, binary alloys, and previously unexplored ternary alloys, encompassing $\approx$1.4 million adsorption configurations on $>$2,600 crystallographically distinct surfaces. Using distribution-based similarity analysis and principal component analysis of AED moments, we identify composition-facet combinations with adsorption landscapes associated with activity and qualitative selectivity trends toward C1 products such as methanol and methane. Our framework links surface structure to adsorption-based catalytic trends, providing experimentally testable composition-facet candidates for further investigation and validation.

items.title: Breaking of clustering and macroscopic coherence under the lens of asymmetry measures
items.summary: In one-dimensional systems, spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) states are fragile by nature, as the injection of a non-zero energy density above the ground state is expected to restore the symmetry. This instability implies that local perturbations can lead to macroscopic correlation profiles, a breaking of clustering properties and even macroscopic quantum superpositions. In this work, we investigate the effect of interaction on this phenomenology by considering an interacting model with conserved domain wall number, that possesses a ferromagnetic ground state breaking the Z2 symmetry of the Hamiltonian. We first show that a local quench in this system amplifies quantum interferences, producing a macroscopic magnetisation profile that directly reflects the scattering phase of the model. Then, we use two asymmetry measures, namely the Entanglement Asymmetry (EA) and Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), to characterise the quantum coherence associated with the fluctuations of the magnetisation. By focusing on subsystems comparable in size to the light-cone of the perturbation, we confirm the emergence of macroscopic quantum coherence throughout the whole perturbed region. Finally, we discuss the link between EA and QFI and show that the variance/EA inequality for pure state can be generalised to a QFI/EA inequality for mixed states.

items.title: Magnetic Reconfiguration Controls Spin Splitting and Spin-Orbit-Coupled Responses in Compensated Magnets
items.summary: Compensated magnets provide a versatile platform for spin-dependent electronic and transport phenomena. Here, we show that magnetic reconfiguration, i.e., selective reversal of local moments without changing the underlying crystal structure, can profoundly transform the nonrelativistic spin splitting and spin-orbit-coupled responses of spin-degenerate antiferromagnets (AFMs), altermagnets (AMs), and compensated ferrimagnets (cFIMs). Strikingly, magnetic configurations with nearly degenerate energies can exhibit qualitatively different spin-split band structures and anomalous Hall responses, allowing a small magnetic-energy scale to produce large changes in physical properties. Combining tight-binding models, oriented spin space group analysis, and first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that converting an AM configuration into cFIM states activates staggered onsite-potential contributions to spin splitting, complementing the anisotropic-hopping mechanism of AMs and removing symmetry-enforced degeneracies. Moreover, cFIM symmetry permits an anomalous Hall response at first order in spin-orbit coupling, in contrast to the higher-order or orientation-constrained responses of corresponding AM states. We demonstrate this regime in Mn2Mo3O8, one of 12 cFIM candidates identified in the MAGNDATA database, and further demonstrate its generality by designing cFIMs from collinear AFMs, exemplified by MnGeO3 and Co2Mo3O8.
