authors: Min She, 敏 佘, Qiang Zhang, 强 张, Zhao An, 钊 安, Fan Lv, 帆 吕, Zhaoyi Liu, 兆亿 刘, Jitao Cao, 济韬 曹, Yuhong Zou, 榆红 邹, Ruikai Pan, 瑞恺 潘, Wenpeng Zhou, 文鹏 周, Han Zhang, 涵 张, Jiangshan Tang, 江山 唐, Feng Wang, 峰 王, Franco Nori, Keyu Xia and 可宇 夏
items.summary: High-sensitivity thermometry is critical for cutting-edge technologies such as gravimeters, quantum clocks, and lithography systems. Although recent transformative advances in resonator-based optical microthermometers achieve high sensitivity, the input and output setups are complex and require precise control, severely limiting their practical applications and achievable footprint. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a fiber-integrated thermometer made of a high-Q optical Fabry–Pérot fiber microcavity, filled with transparent but thermal-sensitive ultraviolet glue. The input and transmitted probe laser fields are coupled to the microthermometer via optical fibers, significantly facilitating operation and minimizing the device size. Combining the large temperature dependence of the ultraviolet glue and the micrometer-scale cavity, sensitive thermometry is achieved by independently measuring the resonance shift or the transmission change. Based on evaluation of equivalent temperature noise of the power spectral density, the resonance-shift method achieves microkelvin-level sensitivity. The fixed-wavelength transmission-change method yields a nanokelvin-level readout-referred equivalent temperature-noise floor at high frequencies using quasi-static response calibration. This low-cost, simple, and fiber-integrated microthermometer holds significant potential for applications in quantum device characterization, biocalorimetry, optoelectronic technologies, and next-generation clocks.

Nanophotonic resonances can strengthen the upconversion channel, but in a single-mode structure may also enhance parasitic pump heating. We introduce a two-cavity non-Hermitian architecture that separates preparation of a lower reservoir state from extraction of the phonon-promoted radiative state. A passive exceptional point, containing no optical gain, is placed in the output branch, where it reshapes the projected final-state optical response; all anti-Hermitian diagonal terms describe radiative leakage, internal absorption, or material decay. For a CdS parameter set, the four-mode calculation gives a 1.23 × 103 enhancement of upconverted photoluminescence relative to a single-mode control, while the pump-induced heat load rises by only 2.8 × 10–3%. The gain consists of a factor of 3.45 × 102 from the independent output resonance and a further factor of 3.56 from exceptional-point tuning.

items.title: Skin-like Prototissues Integrating Pro-Angiogenic Signaling with Antibacterial Barrier Function
authors: Zefeng Wang, Qiyi Li, Xiaohong Zhou, Yan Zhou, Yanwen Zhang, Tianhong Chen, Dinggeng He, Kemin Wang, and Jianbo Liu
items.summary: Abstract The bottom-up assembly of prototissues from synthetic protocells provides a promising route for bridging artificial cell engineering with tissue-level functionality; however, integrating biochemical signaling with adaptive barrier properties within such systems remains challenging. Here, we construct skin-like prototissues by embedding catalytically active coacervate vesicle protocells within a gelatin–hydroxypropyltrimethylammonium chloride chitosan hydrogel. Within this architecture, spatially organized protocells act as confined microreactors that convert endogenous glucose into nitric oxide (NO), establishing a self-sustained pro-angiogenic NO signaling cascade. Concurrently, evaporation-driven surface reorganization generates an epidermis-like hydrophobic interface with antibacterial barrier function. The integration of protocell-mediated NO signaling with matrix-driven antibacterial barrier function yields emergent skin-like functionality. Leveraging this integrated design, the prototissues are configured as bioactive patches that markedly accelerate healing of bacterially infected diabetic wounds by promoting neovascularization while suppressing bacterial colonization. This work establishes a generalizable strategy for translating prototissue architectures into functional therapeutic interfaces.

items.title: Ultrafast Spatiotemporal Control of Dynamic Metasurfaces
authors: Andrea Schirato, Margherita Maiuri, Giulio Cerullo, and Giuseppe Della Valle
items.summary: Abstract Optical metasurfaces have transformed nanophotonics by making space a critical design parameter, allowing the properties of light to be tailored through the geometry and arrangement of subwavelength resonators. Dynamic flat optics extends this paradigm by introducing time as an additional degree of freedom, enabling their optical responses to be reconfigured after fabrication. In this context, ultrafast all-optical metasurfaces stand out as a powerful platform, combining pulsed-laser excitation and nonequilibrium-carrier-mediated nonlinearities to reconfigure resonant responses on femtosecond time scales. However, most demonstrations have focused on temporal modulation alone, treating all-optical control as a primarily temporal process. In this Review, we bridge these frameworks and identify spatiotemporal control as a frontier for dynamic metasurfaces, where photoexcitation is used to engineer transient optical functionalities through spectral, spatial, and temporal structuring of the perturbation. We organize this picture into intra-resonator, compound-meta-atom, and metasurface-aperture regimes, highlighting recent representative works and outlining routes toward flat-optical systems whose functionality can be designed, activated, and dynamically reconfigured across both space and time.

items.title: Nitrate Intercalation Induced Low-Temperature Synthesis of Oxygen-Defective Co 3 O 4 for Scalable Electro-Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
authors: Congcong Jian, Ruixiang Ge, Yang Li, Haiqing Gong, Min Ma, Xinru Yu, Jie Zhao, Ruochen Zhang, Shuo Lu, Shuo Zhang, Suli Li, Hua Zhou, and Jian Tian
items.summary: Abstract Oxygen-defective spinels have been extensively investigated as efficient electrocatalysts for the electro-oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA). Nevertheless, the scaled-up synthesis of oxygen-defective spinels remains challenging. Herein, we report a nitrate intercalation strategy to induce the thermal decomposition of α-Co(OH) 2 precursor at an unprecedentedly low temperature of 150 °C, yielding the oxygen-defective spinel Co 3 O 4 phase. Mechanistic investigations disclose a unique redox chemistry, where the intercalated nitrate anions behave as oxidizing agents to drive the dehydroxylation of the hydroxide precursor. Furthermore, the presented synthetic strategy is readily scalable for the single-batch synthesis of 17.2 g of catalyst, which achieves an industrial-level current of 100 A in a 200 cm 2 continuous-flow reactor, with a corresponding HMF conversion of 93.7% and an FDCA selectivity of 91.3%. This study provides new mechanistic insights into the synthesis chemistry of spinel nanomaterials and paves the way for industrial-scale HMF electro-oxidation.

items.title: Realization of Triangular Antimonene with High In-Plane Fermi Velocities
authors: Bing Liu, Kilian Strauß, Philipp Eck, Jonas Erhardt, Tim Wagner, Manish Verma, Philipp Keßler, Cedric Schmitt, Lukas Gehrig, Stefan Enzner, Vedran Jovic, Chris Jozwiak, Aaron Bostwick, Eli Rotenberg, Timur Kim, Cephise Cacho, Martin Kamp, Domenico Di Sante, Jörg Schäfer, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Simon Moser, and Ralph Claessen
items.summary: Abstract Two-dimensional materials with high Fermi velocities are promising for high-speed electronic and optoelectronic applications, yet experimental realizations beyond graphene remain scarce. Here, we report the successful synthesis of a triangular monolayer of antimony (Sb) on the wide-gap semiconductor SiC. Using combined angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) in combination with density functional theory (DFT), we reveal substrate-engineered orbital filtering that isolates broad-bandwidth, highly dispersive p x and p y bands, yielding a compensated Fermi surface with an ultrahigh Fermi velocity surpassing that of pristine graphene. Linear dichroism in ARPES measurements confirms the orbital polarization of the high-velocity bands. Consistent with triangular lattice physics, a valley Dirac cone emerges deep below the Fermi level because of enhanced Sb band filling. These results establish triangular antimonene as a two-dimensional p -orbital metal with consistently high in-plane Fermi velocities across its Fermi level electronic states.

items.title: Lead Nanoparticles, the Deep-Ultraviolet to Near-Infrared Plasmonic Platform
authors: Michael Foltýn, Michal Kvapil, Kristýna Bukvišová, Tomáš Šikola, and Michal Horák
items.summary: Abstract Among the non-noble metals, lead (Pb) is a material of particular interest for plasmonic applications in the deep-ultraviolet spectral region. However, experimental studies on its plasmonic performance have not yet been conducted. In this work, the dependence of the optical properties of spherical lead nanoparticles on their diameter is demonstrated. The plasmonic performance of chemically synthesized lead nanoparticles is evaluated at the single-particle level by means of a combination of scanning transmission electron microscopy and electron energy loss spectroscopy. Our findings demonstrate that these nanoparticles support localized surface plasmon resonances across the entire spectrum from the near-infrared to deep-ultraviolet region. This range was identified as the most extensive among all plasmonic elemental metals, extending to wavelengths below 200 nm. Consequently, lead nanoparticles exhibit stable plasmonic performance over a remarkably broad wavelength range, thereby substantiating their potential as a multispectral plasmonic platform.

items.title: Governing Ionic Migration via Polaron-like Engineering in Copper Selenide
authors: Hanwen Hu, Chen Li, Xinyu Guo, Ziyang Zhou, Jiawei Song, Zhiyi Sun, Shuowen Bo, Rui Zhang, Xu Zhang, Qinghua Liu, Yan Cheng, Lei Yang, and Kun Zheng
items.summary: Abstract Understanding the atomistic ion–lattice coupling mechanisms in fast ionic conductors is crucial for achieving tunable ion migration behavior, thereby advancing high-efficiency energy storage and conversion technologies. In this study, combining DFT calculations and in situ synchrotron analysis of Cu 2 Se-based materials, we propose a polaron-like coupled ion–lattice–electron picture to understand the mechanism of migration of Cu + ions. Operando XANES and EXAFS reveal that migrating Cu + ions dynamically couple with local lattice distortion and 3d–4p hybridization to form transient polaron-like states, acting as tunable migration “switches”. Through bond contraction and expansion and polaron-like delocalization and localization, the Cu + ion migration barrier can be effectively increased or decreased. The regulated ion migration behavior of Cu + is approved by differential charge distribution analysis and in situ TEM. This polaron-like engineering strategy offers a unified paradigm for precisely governing ionic transport in superionic conductors.

items.title: Chaotropic Solvation Activates a Mobile PVA Interfacial Phase for Adhesive and Low-Impedance Hydrogels
authors: Xiaofeng Pan, Meijie Huang, Tianxue Zhu, Xinlong Shang, Bohao Xu, Yonghao Ni, Dongdong Ye, and Qinhua Wang
items.summary: Abstract The seamless biointegration of hydrogels is hindered by a fundamental physicochemical paradox: bulk stability necessitates conformational constraints within cross-linked networks, whereas interfacial adhesion demands chain mobility for conformal adaptation. Herein, we present a chaotropic solvation-regulated strategy to resolve this conflict. By exploiting the chaotropic effect of thiocyanate anions (SCN – ), we selectively disrupt the hydrogen-bond ordering of poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) phases embedded within a robust polyacrylamide (PAM) framework. This “salting-in” process reprograms the hydration interfacial dynamics, transitioning frozen polymer chains into an active, fluid-like state without compromising the bulk elastic integrity. The resulting hydrogel exhibits a structure–function-coupled synergy, featuring good adhesion (∼75 N/m), low modulus (∼0.046 MPa), and ultralow impedance (∼18 Ω at 100 Hz). Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that chaotropic solvation increases conformational entropy, driving adaptive interfacial rearrangement. Importantly, this unlocking strategy demonstrates broad applicability across polymer backbones, offering a versatile approach for high-fidelity biointerfaces.

items.title: Soft-mode nonlinearities away from ferroelectric phase transition
authors: Payel Shee, Ipek Efe, Jingwen Li, Kshitij V. Goyal, Morgan Trassin, Shovon Pal
items.summary: Terahertz fields can drive soft lattice vibrations associated with ferroelectric phase transitions. These modes are hybrid in character, with a significant predominance of electronic oscillators and local-field effects. By investigating a strained paraelectric SrTiO3 using nonlinear terahertz spectroscopy, Shee et al. show that, though strong local-field effects sustain coherent nonlinear responses, the absence of polarization keeps the system in the perturbative regime of light-matter interaction. The findings offer insights into the role of polarization in controlling nonlinear lattice dynamics.

items.title: Physical understanding of dopant pair interaction and segregation energies in single-atom alloys
authors: Rui Qi, Yan Wang, Yujing Zhang, Sergey V. Levchenko, Xiaojuan Hu, Iftikhar Hussain, Zhong-Kang Han
items.summary: When do isolated dopants in single-atom alloys remain dispersed at surfaces or pair and segregate? Qi et al. combine first-principles calculations with interpretable data mining to identify how guest and host properties jointly govern these competing tendencies. The resulting physical rules guide large-scale alloy screening and connect materials discovery with an interpretable picture of dilute-alloy stability.

items.title: Ferroelectric Polarization Dynamics of HZO FeCAPs at a Verified Subnanosecond Time Scale
authors: Mor M. Dahan, Emanuel Ber, Florian Wunderwald, Guy Orlev, Edan Gefen, Ilya V. Karpov, Thomas Mikolajick, Sou-Chi Chang, Uwe Schroeder, and Eilam Yalon
items.summary: Abstract Ferroelectric random-access memory (FeRAM) based on the ferroelectric capacitor (FeCAP) offers a promising solution for next-generation embedded memory. In this Letter, we demonstrate subnanosecond ferroelectric polarization dynamics in HZO FeCAPs using an RF-compatible structure. By simultaneously measuring the electrode voltage and transient current under subnanosecond pulsing, we directly observe polarization dynamics with a temporal resolution below 100 ps. Our results demonstrate subnanosecond switching under directly monitored TE pulses with voltage amplitudes of 5 V in 8 nm-thick HZO capacitors with an area of 16 μm 2 . We also map switching kinetics for sub-10 ns pulse widths using this methodology. We further correlate polarization obtained from the dynamic current transient with the results from the postpulse readout scheme. Motivated by dynamic random-access-memory (DRAM) latency targets, these results establish a device-level benchmark for delivered subnanosecond switching in HZO FeCAPs and, together with a simplified nucleation-limited switching (NLS) analysis, define an effective ultrafast switching window for FeCAP evaluation.
